To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the E. coli and Salmonella O85 and O17 antigens have the same backbone structure and that O-antigen genes specific to the O85 O- antigen gene cluster can be used for identification and detection.

the E. coli and Salmonella O-antigencs O85 and O17 have closely related polysaccharide structures and that the O85 O- antigen gene cluster contains two genes that can be used for PCR-based detection of E. col O85.
E. coli O84 and Salmonella enteritica O17 are closely related and that the O-antigen of E. coli is more complex and has an O-acetyl substituent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
structural and genetic characterization of E. coli and Salmonella O-antigene, which is of importance for the development of new diagnostic assays.
structural characterization of the O-antigen and the genetic characterization of the O-polysacchardie gene cluster of E coli O85 and its relatedness to the O-antigene of S. enteric O17.
the structural and genetic characterization of a pair of closely related E. coli and Salmonella O-polysacchrides and the development of a PCR-based assay for detection of E. coli O85.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the E. coli and Salmonella O-antigene structures are identical, but that the E. colipolysaccharide lacks the O-acetyl group.
the O85 and O17 O-polysacchrides are very closely related, but not identical.
E. coli O84 and S. enteriaca O17 have identical O-antigene structures and identical O-antigen biosynthesis gene clusters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have characterized a new E. coli O-serogroup, E. coli O84, and a new Salmonella serotype, S. enterica 17:k:z4,5,7,9,12.
E. coli O-antigen genes are more frequently shared among E. coli strains than among S. enterica strains, and that E. coli genes can be present also in the S. enterica genome, but not vice versa.
the O-antigen of S. enterida O17 is closely related to that found in E. coli O84 and E. coli O86, and that the O-85 O-antigene is a new member of the O84/O86 group.
The main takeaway from our work is that
O-antigen structures can be very similar, but still be used to discriminate between closely related bacteria.
the E. coli and Salmonella O-antigene databases need to be updated with the O85- and O17-specific genes and structures, which will help to identify new O-antigentypable strains.
O-antigen genes can be shared between E. coli and Salmonella species, and that O-antigene gene clusters can evolve by the acquisition of new genes.
